weaknesses: Limited generalization scope: Single hardware platform (Unitree H1-2 with Inspire RH56DFTP hands) and single tactile sensor modality (piezoresistive, normal force only). Generalization to other dexterous hands and tactile technologies is entirely unknown.

Incremental algorithmic novelty: Core components (DiT, AdaLN, cross-attention, LoRA) are all existing techniques. The contribution is primarily their combination and modality assignment, which is sensible but engineering-focused rather than providing fundamental algorithmic innovation.

Mixed simulation results weaken generalization claims: LIBERO 94.2% (tied with π0), RoboTwin 2.0 85.3% (3 points behind baselines), UniVTAC 82.1% (behind N0-VTLA). Vision-only DECO does not consistently outperform baselines across benchmarks, suggesting benefits may be task-specific.

Baseline selection concerns: Primary comparisons are against ACT (2023) and DP (2025). Contemporary methods (π0, π0.5) often outperform DECO on simulation benchmarks, and the 21% improvement is relative to weaker baselines with 51-57% base success rates.

Dataset scale is modest: DECO-50 has only 50 hours and 8K trajectories compared to RoboMIND 2.0 (1000+ hours) and Open X-Embodiment (1M+ episodes), though the value lies in the specific modality combination rather than absolute scale.

Weak out-of-distribution generalization: Material sorting Task 2 OOD results show drastic drops (DECO: 4/20 on black mouse vs 20/20 on training objects), suggesting limited robustness to distribution shifts.

UniVTAC tactile improvements are marginal: The tactile adapter only shifts slip failures minimally (6→4 on insert_tube, 37→41 on insert_hole) with 82.1% average unchanged. Insert_HDMI failures remain timeout-based, suggesting the problem may not be solvable by tactile information.

Limited analysis of learned representations: While the paper identifies when tactile helps, deeper analysis of what tactile signal features are learned and how they influence decision-making would strengthen understanding.

Two-stage training justification unclear: No ablation comparing joint training (vision + tactile from scratch) vs. two-stage training is provided, leaving the motivation for the training paradigm implicit.
